sections.h2: How quickly can a College Station house be sold?
sections.html:
A cash contract can close in a few weeks, while a listing usually takes longer but may bring a higher price. Either route works in College Station, and the better one depends on repairs, tenants and your deadline.

The city sits in Brazos County next to Texas A&M University, and that tie shapes who buys and who rents.

  • Cash contract: the house is bought as it stands, and you pick the closing date.
  • Agent listing: the widest audience, with showings and repair requests.
  • Investor sale: similar to cash, common for houses that already have renters.
  • Holding as a rental: legal, but the city requires registration, covered below.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau report about College Station?
sections.html:
It describes a student-heavy city. QuickFacts shows 127,472 residents for July 1, 2025, a 5.8% gain on the April 2020 base, and the owner-occupancy rate for 2020-2024 is just 35.4%.

sections.h2: What else does QuickFacts say about daily life here?
sections.html:
The mean commute is 17.4 minutes, short for Texas, and the city covers 51.16 square miles of land with 2,355.6 residents per square mile at the 2020 count. Only 66.1% of residents lived at the same address a year before, which shows steady churn in student housing.

  • Veterans: 3,601 residents.
  • Under 18: 16.9% of the population.
  • Broadband: 84.6% of households subscribe.
  • Retail sales in 2022: $2,378,837 thousand.

For a seller, turnover means rentals change hands often, and an owner of a house in a student area should expect buyers to ask about the rental registration record.

sections.h2: How did College Station start as a college town?
sections.html:
The city website says Texas A&M, the first state institution of higher education in Texas, was inaugurated in 1876. The Postal Service designated the area College Station in 1877, taking the name from a train station west of campus.

The city was incorporated in 1938 after a petition from 23 men, and voters approved it 217 to 39 on October 19, 1938. College Station became the first general law city in Texas to employ a city manager, and in 1952 voters adopted a home rule charter once the population passed 5,000.

The university enrolls nearly 80,000 students, and the George H.W. Bush Presidential Library and Museum draws more than 125,000 visitors a year, both according to the city. Those facts keep demand for housing tied to the academic calendar.

sections.h2: Must a College Station rental be registered?
sections.html:
Yes, with limits. The city's rental housing page requires registration of every single-family, townhome, duplex, tri-plex, four-plex, five-plex or six-plex dwelling that the owner does not occupy, whether or not rent is charged. Condos and buildings with more than six units are not covered.

The page lists a $90 one-time fee per building as of October 24, 2022, with no yearly renewal. An owner living elsewhere must name a local contact who lives within 30 miles of City Hall and is not on the lease. Late owners pay $25 a day for days 31 to 45 after notice, rising to $100 a day from day 76, and municipal court fines run from $180 to $500 depending on the number of offenses and when they are paid.

Selling a rented house? Ask the city if any penalties are open, because the page says they must be paid before registration can be finished.

sections.h2: Do game-day and family-occupied houses count?
sections.html: They do. The city definition names vacation and game-day rentals and also houses where a relative lives and the owner does not. Collect the registration record before you list, and ask code enforcement whether any separate short-term rental permit applies to your address.

sections.h2: What does the city itself say about living in College Station?
sections.html:
Its About page highlights 58 parks covering 1,900 acres, a regional airport served by major airlines, and highways that put five of the country's 20 largest cities within a three-hour drive. It reports an area unemployment rate of 3.7 percent as of June 2024 and says the property tax rate is among the lowest in Texas.

The page also says the city is working with Texas A&M and the City of Bryan on a high-tech research hub. Parks, a university and a short commute are the features most likely to matter to a buyer, so mention them with the house details.

The page also credits recognition as a family-friendly city in 2024, a claim best treated as the city's own description. Buyers should rely on school and tax documents for the specific address.

sections.h2: How do Brazos County property tax dates work?
sections.html:
The Brazos appraisal district lists January 1 as the valuation date, with notices of appraised value sent in several runs from April 15 to June 1. The protest deadline is May 15, or 30 days after the notice. Rates are set from July to September, and the tax assessor-collector mails bills in October and November.

Statewide, the Comptroller sets the due date at January 31 and the first delinquent day at February 1, with a six percent penalty and one percent interest then. The district is at 4051 Pendleton Drive in Bryan, takes exemption applications by email at an address on its contact page and is open on weekdays.

sections.h2: What does a College Station buyer inherit from the tax year?
sections.html:
A tax lien attaches each January 1, and the Comptroller says the owner on that date is liable even after a sale. Buyers who take title after January 1 may claim a homestead exemption right away if the seller had none. The title company prorates the year, so ask for the tax certificate before you sign.

A delinquent owner can ask the collector to waive penalty and interest, provided the tax is paid within 21 days of learning of the delinquency and the request is made in writing within 181 days after the due date.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited or facing foreclosure?
sections.html:
Probate a will within four years of death, and use a muniment of title when no administration is needed. A foreclosure sale happens on a first Tuesday after a notice of sale, and the State Law Library notes a 20-day window to reinstate after the default notice.

A deed is recorded by the county clerk, which per the Texas Courts manual requires acknowledgment before a notary or two witnesses and prints a fee of $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for every added page.

faqs.q: Do tenants have to register a College Station rental?
faqs.a: No. The city page says tenants are not required to register. The owner is responsible, and an out-of-town owner needs a local contact within 30 miles of City Hall.

faqs.q: What does College Station charge to register a rental?
faqs.a: $90 per building, one time, as of October 24, 2022 according to the city. Late registration adds daily penalties, so register within 30 days of the first notice.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about a Brazos County exemption?
faqs.a: Contact Brazos Central Appraisal District, which lists a phone and email on its contact page. The deadline for most exemptions is April 30.

faqs.q: When is the Brazos County protest deadline?
faqs.a: May 15, or 30 days after the notice of appraised value, whichever is later, as the district's process page states.

faqs.q: Can I sell with a lien for back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, and the title company will order the figures from the tax office.
